original_death.death_reason_verbatim: Dimensionally invalid Nusselt correlation (RHS units m^-1.5 s^-1.5, not dimensionless) AND regime mismatch (20-100 kHz in 2-10 mm channels places the geometry in the incompressible-oscillation regime where streaming is confined to thin boundary layers — bulk convective enhancement cannot follow).

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: The 2026 candidate relied on a dimensionally invalid Nusselt correlation and applied 20-100 kHz acoustic actuation in 2-10 mm channels, a regime where acoustic streaming is confined to thin boundary layers and cannot enhance bulk convective heat transfer.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: At acoustic wavelengths (λ ≈ 7-34 mm in air-equivalent media at 100-20 kHz) much larger than the 2-10 mm cooling channel hydraulic diameter, the acoustic boundary layer thickness δ_ν = √(2ν/ω) exceeds the channel half-height, so Rayleigh/Schlichting streaming momentum is deposited at the wall and decays before reaching the channel core.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: High-frequency (>500 kHz), high-intensity volumetric bulk acoustic sources capable of generating inertial cavitation and microstreaming nuclei distributed throughout the bulk coolant, with wavelengths matched to or smaller than the channel hydraulic diameter.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: Bulk-distributed inertial cavitation microstreaming injects vorticity directly into the channel core rather than relying on viscous penetration from the wall, shifting the operative mechanism from boundary-layer streaming to volumetric microjet-driven turbulent mixing — a fundamentally different convective transport pathway that the 2026 correlation did not represent.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A 2055 battery cooling architecture using megahertz-range phased bulk-acoustic transducer arrays coupled with engineered nanobubble-seeded dielectric coolant to drive volumetric microstreaming inside sub-millimeter bifurcated cold plates bonded directly to 4680-format cells.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: MHz bulk acoustic field nucleates inertial cavitation on seeded nanobubbles | Cavitation microjets inject momentum into the bulk coolant | Volumetric microstreaming replaces molecular diffusion as the dominant transport mode across the channel cross-section | Effective bulk heat transfer coefficient rises independent of Reynolds number, flattening cell-to-cell ΔT during 4C charging
fields.INTERVENTION: Co-integrated (>500 kHz, >50 W/cm²) piezoelectric transducer arrays fabricated by micro-transfer printing onto the floors of additively manufactured aluminum cold plates with 0.5 mm hydraulic-diameter bifurcated channels, filled with a fluorocarbon dielectric coolant pre-seeded with 50-200 nm gas-core nanobubbles at 10⁸-10⁹ mL⁻¹ concentration.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: 40-55% reduction in cell-surface temperature rise during 4C fast charge (from a 2026 baseline of ~18 °C peak ΔT to ~8-11 °C), with cell-to-cell ΔT uniformity improved from ±4 °C to ±1.5 °C; bulk coolant-side heat transfer coefficient target of 15,000-25,000 W/m²·K (2026 baseline 2,500-4,000 W/m²·K).
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Operating frequency 0.5-3 MHz; channel hydraulic diameter 0.3-0.8 mm; coolant dynamic viscosity <5 mPa·s; nanobubble concentration 10⁸-10⁹ mL⁻¹ with radius 50-200 nm; acoustic pressure amplitude >150 kPa at the bubble; coolant temperature 15-55 °C; cell C-rate up to 6C.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: Measured bulk-averaged Nusselt number on a representative cell cooling plate failing to exceed 3× the no-acoustic baseline at matched Reynolds and pumping power within ±10%, across at least three independent test articles.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Quantitative Schlieren/PIV-measured time-averaged streaming velocity in the channel midplane (y/D_h ≈ 0.5) as a function of acoustic drive amplitude, normalized against the bulk cross-sectional RMS velocity.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Micro-particle image velocimetry (μ-PIV) with 200 nm tracer particles on a transparent glass-and-silicon surrogate cold plate of identical hydraulic geometry, paired with high-speed Schlieren imaging to confirm cavitation event density.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Checkable today (2026 µ-PIV) on existing MHz transducer coupons and nanobubble-seeded fluids; full-pack validation checkable by 2030.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Streaming velocity at channel midplane ≥30% of the mean bulk flow velocity at acoustic power densities ≤10 W per channel segment.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Midplane streaming velocity below 10% of bulk mean velocity at any tested drive amplitude below the cavitation threshold of the seeded fluid.

fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: No available in-pack flow-velocity field reconstruction technique could separate acoustic-streaming momentum addition from buoyancy- and baffle-driven convection inside a sealed, acoustically lossy battery enclosure.

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: The physics kill: Darcy's law as cited is invalid at the stated Re > 4000 operating point, and the realistic delta-P penalty for any porous insert that delivers meaningful Nu enhancement makes the technology thermodynamically inferior to the established alternatives.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Darcy's law is invalid at Re > 4000 because inertial turbulence dominates over viscous Darcy flow, so the cited pressure-drop penalty makes any porous insert that delivers meaningful Nusselt enhancement thermodynamically inferior to plain enhanced tubes.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: The Reynolds-scaling mismatch between Darcy's law (Re << 1 in pores) and the actual shell-side operating regime (Re > 4000), where form drag and turbulent dissipation—not viscous resistance—set the pumping cost.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: Pore-scale manufacturing that produces a spatially varying, anisotropic permeability field engineered so that the local pore Re stays in the Darcy-Forchheimer transition window even when the bulk shell Re is 10^4–10^5, combined with active local pumping or phase-change augmentation.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: The original mechanism assumed a uniform porous block whose penalty scaled with bulk flow; a 2055 architecture with engineered permeability gradients and embedded micro-actuators decouples the turbulence-generating structure from the through-flow path, so the energy dissipation per unit Nu enhancement drops by an order of magnitude rather than merely improving a coefficient.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A shell-and-tube exchanger whose shell contains a lattice of additively manufactured, locally anisotropic porous struts with embedded MEMS micro-jets and phase-change microcapsules that inject targeted swirl only where the local bulk Re exceeds the Forchheimer transition.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Engineered anisotropic pore field localizes dissipation to low-Re zones | MEMS micro-jets inject momentum to raise local shear without raising bulk ΔP | phase-change microcapsules add latent heat uptake at hotspots | net Nu rises while shell-side pumping power stays within the 2026 baseline
fields.INTERVENTION: Replace conventional porous inserts with 3D-printed graded-permeability struts carrying embedded micro-jet arrays and phase-change microcapsules tuned to the shell-side flow map.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: Shell-side Nusselt number increase of 120–180% (relative to plain bare tubes) at a shell-side pressure drop no greater than 1.4× the 2026 plain-tube baseline, i.e., a thermal-hydraulic Figure of Merit (Nu/Nu0)/(f/f0)^(1/3) ≥ 2.3.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Bulk shell-side Re 1×10^4 to 1×10^5; fluid: water, ethylene glycol, or supercritical CO2; temperature 40–350 °C; valid for tube-side Re 5×10^3 to 2×10^4.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: Measured (Nu/Nu0)/(f/f0)^(1/3) ≤ 1.4 across the stated Re range with statistically significant sample size (n ≥ 5 replicates).
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Pore-scale local permeability tensor uniformity, measured as the coefficient of variation of the Forchheimer coefficient across a representative strut sample.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Micro-PIV and μ-CT porosity reconstruction on additively manufactured strut coupons, combined with pressure-drop versus flow-rate curve fitting to extract the inertial resistance coefficient.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Checkable now and verifiable at component level by Q2 of the 2030s once multi-material additive platforms mature; full system-level data by the early 2040s.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Coefficient of variation of the Forchheimer coefficient below 8% and a Forchheimer coefficient in the range 0.12–0.18 across the strut lattice.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Coefficient of variation above 15% or mean Forchheimer coefficient above 0.30 at the design pore size, indicating the manufactured part has reverted to the 2026 high-penalty regime.

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: Boundary-condition inversion: the candidate's own stated materials (SS304, Ti-6Al-4V) contradict its own stated effectiveness rule — even if the underlying cryogenic-cooling effect were real, the stated rule fails for the stated materials.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: The candidate's effectiveness rule — "limited effectiveness for materials with low thermal conductivity" — directly inverts for its own flagship materials, since SS304 and Ti-6Al-4V are precisely low-thermal-conductivity alloys, making 0 °C cryogenic cooling mechanically unable to extract heat from the cutting zone.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: Heat flux from the primary shear zone in low-thermal-conductivity alloys (Ti-6Al-4V ≈ 6.7 W/m·K, SS304 ≈ 16 W/m·K) is bottlenecked by conduction through the chip and workpiece, so external coolant at any fixed temperature cannot sustain a sub-flash-temperature tool–chip interface.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: Tool-integrated, actively regulated micro-channel heat extraction with sub-millisecond closed-loop control, allowing heat to be pulled directly from the cutting edge at a rate exceeding the shear-zone heat-generation rate.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: The 2026 mechanism relied on bulk coolant contacting the chip and tool flank to remove heat conductively, which is fundamentally defeated by the low thermal diffusivity of the target alloys; moving the heat sink into the tool body shortens the conduction path by 2–3 orders of magnitude and lets the system actively hold the rake face below the alloy's dynamic recrystallization temperature, eliminating — not merely reducing — the thermal softening step in the chain.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A 2055 cryo-assisted micro-channel insert turning tool with embedded cryogenic micro-evaporators and on-tool thin-film thermopile sensors, governed by a sub-millisecond control loop that modulates two-phase flow to clamp rake-face temperature at a setpoint chosen below the workpiece's dynamic softening threshold.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Shear-zone heat generation in workpiece → conductive extraction through tool insert into internal micro-channel array → two-phase cryogenic boiling absorbs latent heat at near-constant interface temperature → active control loop matches extraction rate to heat-flux profile → tool-edge hardness preserved across the pass
fields.INTERVENTION: Replace standard CNMG insert with a micro-channel carbide insert fed by regulated liquid-nitrogen flow (~110 K, 0.5–2.0 MPa), with closed-loop control from thin-film temperature sensors on the rake face; maintain conventional flood coolant for chip evacuation, but treat it as a secondary heat path only.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: Surface roughness Ra improvement of 55–70% versus dry/mql baseline on Ti-6Al-4V (from ~0.8 µm to ~0.25–0.35 µm) and 40–55% on SS304 (from ~1.2 µm to ~0.55–0.70 µm); flank wear VB reduced by 45–60% over 600 s of cuts at v_c = 120 m/min, f = 0.15 mm/rev, a_p = 1.0 mm.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Valid for carbide inserts capable of withstanding 1.0–1.5 GPa hoop stress at 110 K with internal channel walls ≥ 80 µm; cutting speeds 80–180 m/min on Ti-6Al-4V and 60–140 m/min on SS304; rake-face temperature clamped at 600–750 K for Ti-6Al-4V and 650–800 K for SS304.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: Measured rake-face temperature exceeding the workpiece's dynamic recrystallization threshold (>0.4·T_m, ~723 K for Ti-6Al-4V) for more than 5% of cut time at any feed ≥ 0.15 mm/rev would falsify the heat-extraction premise.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Rake-face peak temperature excursion per spindle revolution, measured by on-tool thin-film thermopile array.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Sub-µs-response thermopile or embedded K-type micro-thermocouples in the insert, sampled at ≥ 100 kHz with synchronized cutting-force and acoustic-emission acquisition.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Verifiable within the first 30–60 seconds of a single turning pass on Ti-6Al-4V at v_c = 120 m/min, before any tool wear accumulates.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Peak rake-face temperature ≤ 700 K with cycle-to-cycle variation ≤ ±15 K, and a force-temperature correlation slope ≤ 5 N/K indicating that heat removal — not plastic dissipation — is the limiting rate.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Sustained rake-face temperature > 780 K for > 2% of the pass, or force-temperature correlation slope > 20 N/K, indicating conduction-limited extraction and confirming that the micro-channel approach has collapsed to the original 2026 failure mode.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Prior art (doi:10.1021/acs.energyfuels.5c04026) already teaches amino-acid-mediated CO2 conversion to solid carbonate, reducing the candidate to a routine glycine-for-amine substitution with no new causal structure.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: The 2026 mechanism relies on bulk aqueous glycine chemistry where CO2 reacts with the amine group of free glycine in solution; the reaction is kinetically gated by the nucleophilicity of the primary amine, which cannot distinguish CO2 from co-existing acid gases (SOx, NOx, HCl) and is poisoned by flue-gas moisture and trace metals that chelate glycine and deactivate it.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: Solid-state enzyme-mimetic CO2 hydratase catalysts embedded in a gas-contacting membrane scaffold that perform biological-style CO2 hydration and bicarbonate fixation at the flue-gas/membrane interface, excluding water vapor and competing acid gases by size and polarity selectivity before bulk chemistry occurs.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: The 2026 mechanism is a homogeneous solution-phase nucleophilic addition; the new architecture moves the rate-limiting step from chemical nucleophilicity to a confined enzymatic active site operating on dehydrated, size-selected CO2, so the causal chain becomes enzymatic rather than amine-chemistry, and selectivity (not bulk amine loading) governs throughput.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A membrane contactor packed with immobilised carbonic anhydrase-mimetic metal-organic-framework (MOF) catalysts that selectively hydrate flue-gas CO2 and precipitate CaCO3 in a dry recycle loop, eliminating bulk amine handling, water co-adsorption, and acid-gas poisoning.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Size/polarity-selective CO2 permeation through hydrophobic membrane pores | enzymatic Zn-OH active site hydrates CO2 to HCO3- at the catalytic interface | HCO3- reacts with Ca2+ delivered from a dry CaO recycle loop to form CaCO3 nanoparticles | CaCO3 is calcined in a separate, impurity-free stream so the flue-gas-contacting loop never sees regeneration acid gases

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: Dimensionally invalid Nusselt correlation (RHS units m^-1.5 s^-1.5, not dimensionless) AND regime mismatch (20-100 kHz in 2-10 mm channels places the geometry in the incompressible-oscillation regime where streaming is confined to thin boundary layers — bulk convective enhancement cannot follow).

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Dimensional invalidity of the Nusselt correlation (non-dimensional RHS) combined with operation in the incompressible-oscillation acoustic regime, where streaming collapses into thin boundary layers and bulk convective enhancement cannot be realized.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: At 20–100 kHz in 2–10 mm channels, the acoustic boundary-layer thickness (δ_ac ≈ √(2ν/ω)) is ~1.9–5.6 μm — far smaller than the channel hydraulic diameter — so Rayleigh/Schlichting streaming cannot couple into bulk mixing.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: A volumetric (non-boundary-layer) acoustic streaming mechanism, achievable only by pushing operation into the compressible / high-amplitude regime where nonlinear effects (nonlinear attenuation, radiation pressure, shock-like waveforms) drive bulk momentum injection.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: Bulk momentum injection changes the governing physics from boundary-layer-confined streaming (which cannot accelerate the core flow) to a body-force-driven recirculation whose length scale is set by the channel, not by δ_ac — so the heat-transfer enhancement is no longer choked by viscous penetration depth.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A 2055 battery cooling stack in which MHz-class, high-amplitude focused phased-array transducers generate nonlinear bulk streaming and acoustic-radiation-pressure-driven vortex ejection inside sub-millimeter dielectric coolant channels.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Nonlinear acoustic saturation and harmonic generation deposit momentum into the bulk fluid | Radiation-pressure-driven streaming and cavitation-microjet ejection generate coherent bulk recirculation | Bulk recirculation raises the spatially-averaged effective Reynolds number of the coolant | Spatially-averaged Nusselt number rises proportionally to the bulk-flow contribution, eliminating the boundary-layer ceiling
fields.INTERVENTION: Embed 1–5 MHz gallium-nitride-on-diamond phased-array transducers (each ≤3 mm × 3 mm) into the cell-to-cell coolant channels, driven at acoustic Mach numbers ≥ 0.05, with the dielectric coolant (e.g., fluorinated ketone) chosen for high saturation threshold.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: 25–45 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹ increase in the spatially-averaged convective coefficient (h_eff), translating to a 12–20 K reduction in peak cell-to-coolant ΔT at 4C fast-charge, bounded below by the requirement that radiation-pressure work not exceed 3% of pack electrical input.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Operating frequency 1–5 MHz; acoustic Mach number ≥ 0.05; channel hydraulic diameter 0.3–0.8 mm; dielectric coolant viscosity ≤ 1.5 mPa·s; saturation-limited, not boundary-layer-limited regime (δ_ac > 0.2 mm).
fields.KILL_CONDITION: Direct particle-image-velocimetry or μ-PIV in an operating sub-millimeter channel at ≥1 MHz showing peak bulk velocities below the Stokes-drift-predicted value by more than 40%, indicating failure to escape the boundary-layer regime.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Ratio of measured bulk streaming velocity (centerline) to the Schlichting-boundary-layer velocity prediction at identical acoustic intensity — a streaming-regime indicator independent of h.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Micro-scale particle-image-velocimetry (μ-PIV) using 200–500 nm fluorescent tracers seeded in a transparent test channel with the actual transducer geometry, gated stroboscopically to the acoustic cycle.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Measurable now (2026–2028) on benchtop dielectric channels; full pack integration data checkable by 2030; 2055 fleet-scale validation by 2040.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Centerline streaming velocity ≥ 60% of the nonlinear-regime (Lighthill/Berktay) prediction, i.e., v_bulk / v_BL_pred ≥ 3× at equivalent input power.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: v_bulk / v_BL_pred < 1.5× (i.e., streaming still confined to boundary layer — the original 2026 failure repeats) OR required acoustic intensity to achieve bulk streaming exceeds the 3% pack-energy budget.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Darcy's law and the Forchheimer-Brinkman-Darcy framework are inapplicable at Re > 4000, so the pressure drop penalty for any porous insert delivering a 30-60% Nu uplift is so large that the second-law efficiency is lower than plain tubes with twisted-tape inserts.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: The viscous-to-inertial transition Reynolds number inside the porous matrix occurs below the Re > 4000 operating window, so the Darcy/Forchheimer resistance coefficient rises nonlinearly with velocity and overwhelms any pumping-power advantage gained from heat transfer enhancement.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: The ability to manufacture porous inserts whose internal pore structure enforces laminar-to-turbent transition at a chosen local pore Reynolds number (Rec,target ≈ 200-400) while presenting negligible form drag to the bulk shell-side flow.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: In 2026 the porous medium was treated as a passive resistance element whose f(Reynolds) was set by the bulk flow; in 2055 the medium becomes a flow-conditioning metamaterial that decouples local turbulence generation from bulk pressure drop by spatially grading permeability, so the causal chain shifts from "more turbulence ⇒ more drag" to "graded microstructure produces turbulent boundary-layer renewal at the tube wall while the bulk stream remains effectively inviscid-like."
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A shell-and-tube exchanger whose shell side is filled with a 2055 multi-scale architected lattice (microporous nodes nested inside millimetric graded-permeability struts) that is topology-optimized for simultaneous pore-scale turbulence injection and bulk-stream streamline preservation, combined with on-board MEMS differential-pressure sensing that adaptively bypasses the lattice at high Re.

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: The candidate's own Esw equation shows the absolute switching-loss benefit of DPWM is smallest precisely at the light loads (0.3-0.6 pu) where the candidate claims it is most effective — the baseline-advantage claim inverts at its own claimed operating point.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: The DPWM energy-per-switching formula E_sw shows the per-cycle switching-loss benefit is proportional to the number of clamped devices and the load-dependent dwell time, both of which shrink toward light load, so the absolute watt saving is minimum exactly in the 0.3–0.6 pu region where the 2026 candidate marketed the maximum benefit.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: Absolute switching loss is the product of switching energy per transition and number of transitions, but junction-temperature rise is a thermal integral over time — at 0.3–0.6 pu the device conduction current is too low to create a large thermal margin, so even a 40% fractional cut in E_sw only removes a few watts that the heatsink already absorbs without derating.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: Junction-temperature-aware (or mission-profile-aware) adaptive modulation that reduces switching frequency AND redistributes the switching instants onto the phase leg with the lowest instantaneous junction temperature, rather than statically clamping phases based only on flux angle.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: The 2026 mechanism short-circuits the causal chain by mapping PWM pattern directly to "switching loss," ignoring that lifetime is governed by ΔT_j cycling, not by joules per cycle; the 2055 mechanism intervenes on the actual rate variable (thermal swing amplitude and frequency) so the intervention is causally upstream of the failure mode rather than downstream of a loss term that doesn't couple to lifetime.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A real-time, junction-temperature-sensed, model-predictive hybrid discontinuous-continuous modulator that jointly schedules modulation index, switching frequency, and clamped-phase selection to minimize ΔT_j-weighted switching energy over a horizon.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Online Tj sensing per device → model-predictive scheduler minimizes Σ(E_sw·exp(α·Tj)) over horizon → frequency and clamp pattern adapt to current thermal headroom → ΔT_j cycling amplitude drops, extending lifetime at light-to-medium load

fields.INTERVENTION: Deploy a physics-informed neural loss model on the NPC inverter's gate-drive and modulation controller to co-optimize switching frequency, dead-time, and motor flux setpoint against 1-second-horizon irradiance forecasts on solar-PV-fed induction-motor drives using WBG devices.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: 2.5-4.5% absolute improvement in end-to-end inverter+drive efficiency at partial load (e.g., from ~94.5% to ~97-99%), corresponding to ~7-12% relative loss reduction in the non-MPPT loss budget; honest bound because it is bounded by residual I²R, switching, and magnetic losses.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Valid in PV-fed induction-motor drives with NPC topology at 10-100% load, irradiance 200-1000 W/m², ambient -10 to 50°C, switching frequency 20-100 kHz on GaN/SiC, with forecast horizon 1-10 s and model update <1 ms.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: End-to-end efficiency gain measured against a calibrated, MPPT-saturated baseline below 1.5% absolute across the full load-irradiance envelope; or demonstrated failure of the loss model to outperform fixed dead-time compensation by a statistically significant margin.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Switching-and-harmonic loss component (P_sw + P_h) extracted from a calibrated calorimetric or input-output subtraction at a fixed operating point, normalized to apparent power.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Precision power analyzer (e.g., Yokogawa WT5000 class) differential measurement between the proposed controller and a fixed-dead-time MPPT-saturated baseline, with thermal corroboration via embedded RTDs/thermocouples on the NPC and motor stator.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Checkable on any commissioned solar-PV-driven NPC-inverter motor testbed within 6-12 months of deployment.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Reduction of P_sw + P_h by 30-50% at partial load relative to the fixed-dead-time baseline, with no statistically significant regression in THD-i or torque ripple.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Less than 15% reduction in P_sw + P_h, or any regression >0.3% in THD-i/torque ripple, falsifies the loss-model co-optimization premise.

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: Prior-art anticipation: six independent CMP records (notably doi:10.31274/etd-180810-313 and doi:10.1016/b978-0-12-821791-7.00099-x) already teach MRR-variation modeling for CMP process control with richer dynamics than the candidate's ARX proposal.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Prior-art anticipation by six independent CMP records that already teach MRR-variation modeling for process control, exceeding the candidate's ARX-based stochastic proposal in dynamical richness.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: Stochastic ARX-class models treat MRR variation as an exogenous, scalar-distributed disturbance; the underlying causal driver — the spatially resolved, transient contact-mechanics state between pad, slurry film, and wafer asperities — remains unobserved and unmodeled, so the model can only correlate symptoms rather than intervene on cause.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: Real-time, in-situ, wafer-scale tomographic sensing of the pad-wafer interfacial pressure and slurry film thickness distribution at sub-millisecond cadence, combined with differentiable physics surrogates capable of inverting that field into contact-mode classification and forward-predicted MRR.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: Sensing the actual causal state (interfacial pressure field and slurry film topology) flips the architecture from observation-of-output to intervention-on-cause: control inputs (downforce profile, slurry flow, pad conditioning rate) are now dispatched against predicted contact-mode transitions rather than against a statistical residual, so the same disturbance is suppressed at its physical origin instead of being reacted to after MRR has already drifted.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A closed-loop, physics-inverted CMP controller that fuses wafer-scale interfacial pressure tomography with a differentiable contact-mechanics surrogate, using gradient-based receding-horizon optimization to drive the contact state to a precomputed MRR-invariant manifold in real time.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Interfacial pressure and slurry film field sensed at sub-ms cadence | differentiable contact-mechanics surrogate inverts the field into current contact-mode class and forward-predicts MRR trajectory | receding-horizon optimizer selects downforce/flow/conditioner actuation to drive the predicted trajectory onto the MRR-invariant contact manifold | wafer-level MRR variance collapses because the underlying contact state is held at a known insensitive operating point
fields.INTERVENTION: Deploy pad-embedded capacitive/ultrasonic sensor arrays, high-speed slurry-film optical interferometry, and an on-tool differentiable contact-mechanics solver that issues setpoint trajectories to the downforce, slurry, and conditioner actuators every millisecond.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: Wafer-level within-die MRR standard deviation reduced to 0.4–0.8% of target (from a 2026 typical of 3–6%) for 300 mm logic wafers, corresponding to a 6–12× reduction in post-CMP dishing variation sensitivity; upper bound assumes pad-sensor SNR and solver latency targets are met, lower bound assumes partial sensor coverage.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: 300 mm wafer CMP on porous polyurethane pads with colloidal silica slurry, platen speeds 30–120 rpm, downforce 1–6 psi, slurry flow 100–400 mL/min, pad temperature 20–60 °C, with the contact-manifold assumption holding when asperity-scale wear is the dominant MRR driver rather than bulk slurry chemistry drift.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: A controlled run in which the closed-loop controller is activated on wafers with known step disturbances (downforce and slurry transients) and fails to reduce the within-wafer MRR standard deviation below 1.5% of target across 25 wafers at p<0.01 versus an open-loop baseline.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Pad-wafer interfacial pressure-field map reconstruction error against a reference profilometry scan, measured on production tool test wafers.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Capacitance/ultrasonic pad-sensor array cross-referenced with ex-situ wafer-height profilometry on a sampled wafer subset, logging the L2 reconstruction error per revolution.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Checkable quarterly on a qualified production CMP tool, with the first 12-month cohort providing the trend.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Mean L2 interfacial-pressure reconstruction error trending below 3% of the local pressure range, sustained over 8 consecutive weeks.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Sustained reconstruction error above 7% of the local pressure range for 4 consecutive weeks, or any week in which the controller-on vs. controller-off MRR sigma difference is statistically indistinguishable.

original_death.death_reason_verbatim: doi:10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123235 and doi:10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123384 directly teach electrical signature analysis for wind turbine defect detection in 2025, destroying the novelty claim.

fields.WHAT_KILLED_IT: Two 2025 IEEE papers (DOIs 10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123235 and 10.1109/eic63069.2025.11123384) already taught electrical signature analysis for wind turbine bearing defect detection, destroying the novelty of the proposed mechanism.
fields.PREVENTING_CONSTRAINT: Electrical signatures are a low-amplitude, load-dependent, path-integrated secondary effect of mechanical vibration; they cannot independently localize the bearing component at fault, cannot disambiguate bearing races from gears, and lose sensitivity below operational load — so the 2026 mechanism was structurally bounded to post-hoc confirmation rather than early-stage predictive detection.
fields.REMOVING_CAPABILITY: A non-contact, per-component, load-independent mechanical observable that directly couples to the specific micro-geometry of the bearing raceway, allowing each bearing element to be interrogated individually rather than inferred from terminal electrical noise.
fields.WHY_CAUSAL_CHANGE: Replacing an electrical terminal measurement (a downstream, load-modulated aggregate) with a direct mechanical interrogation of the bearing raceway inverts the causal direction: defects are now the *cause* of a measurable signal rather than a *consequence* inferred through load-current modulation, which is a different causal architecture, not a refinement of the same one.
fields.NEW_ARCHITECTURE: A contactless acoustic-phonon Doppler vibrometry array that fires frequency-modulated coherent phonons through the nacelle air gap and Doppler-demodulates raceway-scattered returns to extract per-element micro-displacement spectra from every bearing in the drivetrain simultaneously, fusing those spectra into a real-time raceway-condition model.
fields.MECHANISM_CHAIN: Coherent phonon pulse illuminates bearing raceway through air gap | Raceway micro-defect scatters phonon with defect-characteristic Doppler sidebands | Phonon return is coherently demodulated per bearing element to extract sub-nm displacement spectra | Raceway spectral fingerprints feed a physics-informed model that predicts remaining useful life before macroscopic fault signatures appear
fields.INTERVENTION: Deploy nacelle-mounted phased phonon transducer arrays on each drivetrain bearing housing that perform continuous FMCW phonon Doppler vibrometry, with edge inference for raceway defect classification.
fields.PREDICTED_EFFECT: 70-90% detection of seeded inner- and outer-race defects at 0.5-1.5 mm length with <10% false positive rate at 95% confidence, achieved 200-400 operating hours earlier than vibration-based methods, across the full 5-100% power operating envelope.
fields.BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS: Wind speeds 3-25 m/s, ambient temperature -20 to +45 °C, nacelle acoustic noise up to 110 dB SPL, bearing speeds 5-1800 rpm; effective where phonon coupling loss through the housing-air interface stays below ~60 dB.
fields.KILL_CONDITION: A controlled seeded-defect trial showing that phonon Doppler vibrometry fails to detect inner-race spalls under 2 mm before catastrophic failure occurs, or that coupling loss exceeds 70 dB in field deployment at more than 30% of turbine sites.
fields.LEADING_INDICATOR: Demonstration of sub-nanometer displacement resolution through a steel bearing housing at standoff distances of 0.5-2 m in a laboratory setting.
fields.MEASUREMENT_METHOD: Bench test using a calibrated bearing with seeded raceway defects, a phased phonon array at 1 m standoff, and laser Doppler vibrometer ground truth; resolution is read as the noise floor of the demodulated displacement spectrum.
fields.MEASUREMENT_WINDOW: Checkable in laboratory today (2026) and field-pilotable by 2030.
fields.EXPECTED_SIGNAL: Displacement spectral noise floor below 0.5 nm/√Hz in the 1-50 kHz band through a 15 mm steel housing.
fields.FAILURE_THRESHOLD: Noise floor above 2 nm/√Hz through the same housing, or inability to resolve defect sidebands above the noise floor at any standoff beyond 0.3 m.
